seo.title: Weird Prediction Markets Report: 131 Days of Data | Dollar Bets
seo.meta_description: 707 markets, 131 days, one board. We crunched our own archive to find the longshots, the lingerers, and the wildest odds swings in weird prediction markets.

summary: 76.8% of the 707 markets that ever hit our board showed up exactly once and vanished forever. This report mines 131 days of our own daily snapshots to find the six $2,000 longshots, the 62-day moon-landing holdout, and the UFO-files market that swung 62 points in six days.
quick_answer: Our 131-day archive of 707 unique markets shows the board is dominated by churn — 76.8% of markets appear only once — while a small cluster of slow-moving Science/Climate markets like the NASA Moon landing bet (62 days) linger far longer than anything else. Six markets hit the steepest payout tier recorded, $1 pays $2,000.

body.content: Here's the number that stopped us mid-scroll: 76.8% of everything that's ever made our board — 543 markets out of 707 — showed up exactly once and never came back. One day in the sun, then gone. That's not a bug in our tracking. That's just what the internet's weirdest dollar wagers actually do.

This report comes entirely from our own daily board snapshots — 131 days of them, April 25 through October 3, 2026, covering 707 unique markets across 1,307 total board slots. Nobody licensed us this data and nobody else has it, because nobody else is screenshotting the same curated top-10 every morning.
the longshots that made the cut

Ten markets on our board paid out at odds steep enough to make a casino blush, and six of them hit the same number on the nose: $1 pays $2,000. A Georgia GOP Senate longshot. A three-day Elon tweet-count bet. WTI crude supposedly touching $175. A Bitcoin price-at-3AM market. An Ethereum coin-flip dressed up as a market. And "Primetime opens to $22 million or more."

content: Georgia nominee bet: "a lottery ticket filing for office"
Bitcoin-at-3AM bet: "someone set an alarm for this exact moment"
Lebanon's Taqaddom Party ($666.67 payout): "Hezbollah pivoting to competitive pickleball"
Solana crash to $70: "Challenger deep has an easier floor to hit"

body.content: Every single one of the six $2,000-payout markets lasted exactly one day on the board. That's the pattern with the truly absurd stuff — it's not built to linger, it's built to make you do a double take and move on.

While hundreds of markets flamed out in 24 hours, a handful refused to go away. The moon landing market — "Will NASA land a person on the Moon before 2028?" — sat on the board for 62 days, the longest run in the entire archive, captioned "one small bet for man." Right behind it: Starship reaching Mars before 2030 (23 days), Taylor Swift getting a papal audience (20 days), and two earthquake markets logging 19 and 18 days.

What's notable about this list: it skews heavily Science and Technology and Climate and Weather — the stuff that's slow-moving by nature, where the news doesn't resolve itself in a week. Those markets don't need a daily headline to stay relevant.
one-day wonders, or: the churn problem

That 76.8% one-day share isn't just a quirk of the longshot list — it's the dominant behavior of the entire board. Our board is explicitly built to surface whatever's weirdest or most relevant that day, so high churn is the design working as intended, not a glitch. Check back next week and you won't see the same ten markets.

Some markets didn't just show up and disappear — they had a full emotional arc. The biggest mover in the archive: "Trump drops more UFO files this month," which went from 3% to 65% in six tracked days, a 62-point swing. Close behind, a single-season receiving yards record market swung 46 points in three days, and "Humans on Mars before 2050" drifted nearly 39 points over months rather than days.

Our board started small — just 58 slots in April — then scaled up to a steady 300 slots a month through May and June before settling into a lower, choppier rhythm for the back half of the year. Median volume per market roughly tripled from April's $8,108 to a peak of $25,285 in June, the same month that produced three of our six $2,000 longshots.

Our board is a curated daily top-10 (sometimes up to 30 slots), hand-picked for being interesting — this measures what made our board, not the full universe of every prediction market that exists. Coverage also has gaps: 12 days missing after July 25, 3 after August 11, and a 14-day gap after August 26. Payouts shown are illustrative snapshots from the dates listed, not current or guaranteed prices.

faqs.q: Why do so many markets only last one day?
faqs.a: Because the board is designed to surface what's freshest and weirdest each day, not to run a fixed leaderboard. With 707 unique markets across 131 days, most are one-and-done by construction — that's 76.8% of the whole archive.

Markets where $1 would have paid out the most if they'd resolved yes at the price we recorded — in this dataset, that tops out at $2,000, a tier reached by six different markets across Other and Crypto categories.

faqs.q: Why did some markets swing so hard in price?
faqs.a: Markets move when new information or sentiment shifts fast — a UFO-files market jumping from 3% to 65% in six days reflects a real news cycle, not a glitch in our tracking. We log the price on the day we snapshot it, a point-in-time read, not a live feed.

faqs.q: Is this the same thing as Dollar Bets' daily board?
faqs.a: No — the daily board is today's curated picks. This report is the aggregate history behind it: 131 days of snapshots turned into first-party research on how our own board behaves over time.
